title: Day and night parts of summer warming did not explain weak bird thermal tracking on 3,960 US survey routes (1966-2025); only day heat changed the bird temperature index from year to year
abstract: Question: bird community temperature indices (CTI) of the North American Breeding Bird Survey (BBS) follow only a small part of their spatial temperature slope in time. All earlier tests used mean temperature. Nights warmed faster than days in summer. Do birds sort by day maxima (Tmax) or night minima (Tmin), and does a day/night benchmark explain the gap? Data: 107,922 standard BBS runs on 3,960 contiguous-US routes (470 species, 1966-2025), NOAA nClimGrid monthly Tmax, Tmin and precipitation (about 5 km). Method (plan written before outcomes): cross-fitted CTI; spatial partial slopes of route CTI on Tmax and Tmin climatology, continental and inside 2 and 1 degree blocks; temporal models with route and observer fixed effects on route warming trends (slow) and anomalies (fast); 300-draw 4 degree block bootstrap. Results: May-July Tmin rose 0.277 C per decade and Tmax 0.187 (East 0.30 against 0.15). Spatial partial slopes were 0.24 (Tmin) and 0.14 (Tmax) with precipitation (difference CI -0.21 to +0.05), and 0.15 and 0.12 inside 2 degree blocks, so neither hypothesis met the pre-specified rule. The day/night benchmark gave an expected CTI trend of 0.093 C per decade against 0.090 for mean temperature; it closed -4.7% of the gap (CI -10.6% to +3.0%). The observed trend stayed 0.023 (25-43% of expectation). A pooled slow slope larger for Tmax (0.085 against 0.020) was an East-West artefact: with regional year effects or inside regions the night slope was equal or larger. Year-to-year, only Tmax anomalies changed the CTI (0.0093, SE 0.0013; Tmin 0.0004, SE 0.0024) in all variants, with a previous-summer carry-over (+0.0033) and a null next-summer placebo. Species did not transfer either part. Conclusion: a wrong climate variable does not cause the weak tracking. Day heat has a fast, partly persistent effect; night temperature carries much spatial sorting but no year-to-year effect. Limitations: correlational design, collinear Tmax and Tmin, monthly means, no detection model, exploratory robustness tests.
